assessments.reasoning: The printed-page 389 single-node discussion conditions stable storage writes on top-action commit and limits necessary writes to stable objects modified by the action. It describes starting a process after a crash to recreate volatile objects.

challenge.method: Checked adjacent recovery details on printed pages 390–391 for lower-level commits, loss of volatile state, and what occurs when recovery itself aborts.
challenge.results: The authors describe writing new versions of stable-reachable objects at top-level commit. The last committed stable state is restored. The volatile recovery process can retry after a failed recovery action.

limitations: The paper presents a modeled crash-recovery design. It describes recovery with high probability and limits robustness claims about effects outside the system.
